verdict_reason: YES, GREEN with confounds is the right axis call, and I checked both halves before saying so. The estimator computes exactly its documented definition -- Jaccard overlap of the top-k cosine neighbourhoods of each sampled vocabulary row between the embedding matrix and a seeded perturbation of it whose realized relative size is exactly noise_std. The `norm + 1e-10` -> `safe_unit_rows` change is VALUE-PRESERVING on real embeddings, measured directly: over gpt2, distilgpt2, pythia-70m and Qwen2.5-0.5B (V up to 151936) the maximum absolute difference between the two unit-row matrices is 5.96e-08 / 5.96e-08 / 7.45e-08 / 4.47e-08 and the maximum RELATIVE difference is 3.28e-07 / 3.35e-07 / 4.63e-07 / 3.50e-07 -- i.e. float32 rounding only. The reason is visible in the same measurement: the smallest embedding row norm on any of the four is 3.5457e-04 (pythia-70m), seven orders of magnitude above the 1e-10 the old code added, and NO row on any model has a norm below 1e-6. So the change is correct in principle (it removes an absolute constant from a scale-free operation) and inert in practice on these checkpoints, which is exactly what a correctness fix should look like. Nothing about the DEFINITION is at fault, so the sample-size problem belongs on `confounds`, not here.
comparable_reason: The metric is a Jaccard index in [0,1] and is width-independent by construction now that the perturbation direction is normalised, so it is comparable in units. The limit is resolution. Ten seeds each, gpt2 vs distilgpt2, seeds 1-10: at the OLD study num_samples=100, gpt2 mean 0.950191 sd 0.002706 range 0.009316, distilgpt2 mean 0.956771 sd 0.003613 range 0.010566, cross-model difference 0.006581 -- the within-model RANGE (0.0093-0.0106) exceeds the between-model difference (0.0066), and the reported SEM is 0.003903, 59% of the effect. At the NEW num_samples=2000: gpt2 mean 0.951742 sd 0.001052 range 0.003110, distilgpt2 mean 0.957135 sd 0.000989 range 0.003367, difference 0.005393, SEM 0.000855 -- now the within-model range is BELOW the difference and the effect is 6.3 SEM. So the 100 -> 2000 raise is measured to fix the power problem. YELLOW, not GREEN, because the whole two-model spread is still only 0.005 on a [0,1] scale, so this metric separates models by less than 1% of its own range.
github_reason: The repository released with the cited inspiration (Wendlandt, Kummerfeld & Mihalcea 2018, arXiv:1804.09692) computes stability as the percentage overlap of the top-10 nearest neighbours between two INDEPENDENTLY TRAINED embedding spaces. It has no noise-perturbation mode, so there is no head-to-head number to run against BLME's self-vs-noised-self construction. I did verify the transform relation algebraically: for two k-NN sets of equal size k with overlap o, |A and B| = o and |A or B| = 2k - o, so Jaccard = o/(2k - o) exactly -- a correct monotone reparameterisation of the paper's o/k. PARTIAL: found and read, not runnable on this estimand.
paper_reason: Wendlandt et al. report stability percentages for word2vec/GloVe/PPMI on PTB/NYT across independently trained spaces, a different experiment. Moreover the per-item monotone transform does not preserve AGGREGATE ranking: overlap profiles [0, 1] and [0.6, 0.6] rank 0.5 < 0.6 under mean-overlap but 0.5 > 0.4286 under mean-Jaccard at k=10, so their published means cannot be recovered from BLME's mean even in principle. BLME's own metadata marks the task proxy-only rather than claiming their numbers.
confounds_reason: This is where the finding belongs. The estimator is sound and the realized perturbation is exactly noise_std at every width, but the shipped protocol at num_samples=100 could not resolve the models it was asked to rank: within-model seed range 0.0093 (gpt2) and 0.0106 (distilgpt2) against a between-model difference of 0.0066. My seeds 1-10 give NO ordering flips at either sample size (the ledger reports 1 flip in 10 with a different seed set), so I do not reproduce the flip -- but the range-exceeds-effect fact reproduces cleanly, and that alone means a 100-row run cannot support a ranking. At 2000 rows the SEM is 0.000855 against a 0.005393 effect, so the study config now clears the bar. The task's new _meta_stability_sem is the right instrument and its warning threshold (0.002) fires at 100 rows (SEM 0.0039) and not at 2000 (0.00086), which is the correct behaviour.
defects: CONFIG (fixed in the study config, still wrong in the package): defaults.yaml ships num_samples: 5000, the study now uses 2000, but any caller who runs the task with num_samples ~ 100 gets SEM 0.0039 on an effect of 0.0054 with nothing but a log line to say so. The _meta_stability_sem emission is the right fix and it is present.

CODE: the absolute-epsilon pattern the source comment criticises is still present TWICE in the same function, in the noise construction rather than the normalisation: `row_scale = E1_float.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-10)` and `raw.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)`. Inert on the four models I measured (minimum row norm 3.5457e-04) but it is the identical hazard, and safe_unit_rows_torch already exists in the same package.

CODE (latent, reference mode): reference_model_path alignment checks only vocabulary LENGTH (`if len(E2_np) != n_vocab`). Two tokenizers with the same vocab size but different id ordering would be compared row-for-row and score near zero rather than near one. Alignment must be by token STRING.

CODE (latent): k is not validated against 1 <= k < V. k=0 makes np.argsort(sims)[-0:] return the WHOLE vocabulary (Python's [-0:] == [0:]) and k >= V re-includes the query despite the -inf self-mask; both produce finite, meaningless values.

CODE: one perturbation draw IS the measurement. stability_std is dispersion across sampled token ids, not across perturbation replicates, and _meta_stability_sem inherits that -- it is the standard error of the row-average at a FIXED noise draw, not of the statistic across draws. The seed sweep above shows the across-draw sd at 2000 rows is 0.00105, slightly larger than the within-run SEM of 0.00086, so the emitted SEM mildly understates the true uncertainty.

CODE (cosmetic): `stability_mode` = 'embedding_noise' and `diagnostic_semantics` = 'embedding_neighborhood_jaccard_stability' are constant strings emitted unprefixed; the same class of column was demoted to _meta_ in sibling tasks.

CONFIG: the shipped reference_model_path=null means the production path never exercises the reference-model branch, so the only mode the study measures is the synthetic-noise proxy. Worth stating in the paper text rather than leaving to metadata.
fix: Keep the current estimator; it is correct and the normalisation change is measured value-preserving to 4.6e-07 relative. Then: (1) average over >= 5 perturbation draws and report the across-draw sd, since one draw is currently the whole measurement and the across-draw sd (0.00105 at n=2000) exceeds the emitted within-run SEM (0.00086); (2) replace the two clamp_min absolute floors with safe_unit_rows_torch; (3) align reference-mode rows by token string and error out when tokenizers differ; (4) validate 1 <= k < V; (5) prefix the two constant strings with _meta_.
